etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English vysual, from Old French, from Late Latin visualis (“of sight”), from Latin visus (“sight”), from videre (“to see”), past participle visus; see visage.

definitions.definition: Related to or affecting the vision.

quote.citation: 2013 May-June, William E. Conner, “An Acoustic Arms Race”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 3, pages 206–7:
quote.text: Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close […] above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them. Many insects probably use this strategy, which is a close analogy to crypsis in the visible world—camouflage and other methods for blending into one’s visual background.

definitions.definition: Any element of something that depends on sight.

quote.citation: 2016, S. C. Sterling, Teenage Degenerate, page 5:
quote.text: It wasn't the first time I pulled an all-nighter, but normally I was coming off an acid trip and still seeing visuals dancing around in my head.

definitions.definition: An image; a picture; a graphic.
(in the plural) All the visual elements of a multimedia presentation or entertainment, usually in contrast with normal text or audio.
(marching band) Any element of a show done by a marching band besides the marching and playing of instruments.
